title: If bare knowledge were the privilege, Rome's own theology books already destroy it
source_text: XXXI. Quod si habeatur ratio prioris istius notitiae, quae tota in simplici quadam apprehensione posita est, certe ut illa quoque Ecclesiae propria maneret, nec infideles ulli ejus participes essent, doctrina Christiana a nullo unquam debuit scripto mandari, ac chartis committi, sed viva tantum voce in Ecclesia perpetuo tradi. At quamvis Pontificii praetendant non omnia fidei mysteria ab Apostolis & viris Sanctis scripta esse, fatentur tamen illa in quamplurimis Doctorum suorum libris scripta reperiri, idque sigillatim, clare & dilucide, ut a legente quovis percipi possint. Ac proinde, quamvis infideles ex scriptis Propheticis & Apostolicis non possent totam doctrinam Christianam haurire, facile tamen illam discere possunt ex Theologorum Christianorum libris. Et sic non minus concidit imaginarium istud Ecclesiae privilegium, quam si omnia in libris Prophetarum & Apostolorum perscripta sint, sicut nos contendimus.
pass_a_gloss: But if account is taken of that former knowledge, which is wholly placed in a certain simple apprehension, certainly that it also might remain proper to the Church, and that no unbelievers might be partakers of it, Christian doctrine ought never to have been committed to writing by anyone, and put on papers, but only handed down forever by living voice in the Church. But although the Pontificians pretend that not all the mysteries of the faith were written by the Apostles and holy men, they nevertheless confess that those things are found written in very many books of their Doctors, and that one by one, clearly and lucidly, so that they can be perceived by any reader. And therefore, although unbelievers could not draw the whole Christian doctrine from the Prophetic and Apostolic writings, yet they can easily learn it from the books of Christian Theologians. And thus that imaginary privilege of the Church falls no less than if all things are written through in the books of the Prophets and Apostles, as we contend.
pass_b_english: If privilege were mere textbook grasp, nothing should ever have been written — only perpetual oral handoff.
Rome already admits the mysteries sit clear in countless scholastic books.
Unbelievers can learn the system from those theologians even if they miss it in the Prophets and Apostles.
So their imaginary privilege dies either way — written Scripture or written Doctors.
